author: fester
body: Each kernel is namespaced (its own bind group and a name prefix on its bindings) so multiple kernels coexist in one module without binding or identifier collisions.

author: fester
body: A buffer argument passed to a helper becomes a storage pointer: inside a kernel (kprefix set) the buffer is a module binding, so pass its address; inside a helper (kprefix empty) the buffer is already a pointer parameter, so pass it through by name.

author: fester
body: wgsl-body emits a statement block for a function or kernel body. Let bindings become WGSL let statements; a tail if becomes structured if/else; a tail device-store becomes an assignment; any other tail becomes a return (for helper functions) or a bare store (for kernels).

author: fester
body: Scan a kernel body for the parameter names used as the base (first argument) of a device-load or device-store. Those parameters are the storage buffers.

author: fester
body: Buffer (pointer) parameters are loop-invariant: they are not vars and are not reassigned on the tail call, so skip their move temp and their move assign.

author: fester
body: A loop iteration whose body is an act block (e.g. a buffer-reading fold that device-loads other elements each step): each act bind becomes a `let`, and the final statement is processed as the loop tail so a self-call still becomes a parallel-move + continue.

author: fester
body: Only helper functions transitively called from a kernel are emitted, so unused foreword glue (thread-index accessors and the like, pulled in by cites) never lands in the shader module as invalid WGSL. Kernel-less modules fall back to emitting every helper.
